notes:
I read brief.md, the critic report r6.md and r4.md (what lies west of x 412) in full. I did not open the repo or rerun the designers' checkers, so each design's geometry claim of 0 failures is taken as reported.

Owner-fit deciders:
1. Cake at the end. The owner has a standing GT rule: "the cake with the princess at the end". A keeps the Torta at local x 148, 650 studs short of the new east edge, and A itself lists this as its main open risk. That is the biggest owner-fit miss of the three.
2. River width at the head. PD3 sets 50..120. A's points 2 and 3 (24 and 40 wide) fall below it. B is fully inside the range. C is inside it but sits at the low end (50..64) in the west.
3. Mouth placement. B's mouth ends at world x 412 on the west edge, beside the hub's apron (east edge 388) and the hub's bounding box (east edge 387). There is no cloud wall there, so the river visibly stops at an open edge near the entrance. A and C both pour into the east cloud wall, which reads as "reaching the far end".
4. Today's look. Today's river is a barrier that players cross by bridge, by wading or by raft. Only C keeps that structure (the entrance and the cake on opposite banks, a bridge that never breaks on the avenue). B keeps it with more complexity. A drops it for most players.

On fun alone, B is the most ambitious, but it is harder for kids to read and it rearranges much of the west map the owner already approved. C does exactly what was asked with the least surprise. Grafting B's reward lean, its bigger waterfall and its edge walls, plus A and B's liquid clip, closes most of C's gaps.
